common_pests_and_diseases.name: Tomato Leaf Curl Virus (ToLCV)

Avoid overhead irrigation

leaf_characteristics.shape: Linear-lanceolate flat blades

stem_characteristics: Erect, hollow tillering culms up to 1.2 meters with auricles and ligules
flower_characteristics: Terminal distichous compact spike (earhead) with multi-flowered spikelets
fruit_characteristics: Ovoid caryopsis (grain) with ventral crease, amber or reddish brown
growth_habit: Annual temperate-subtropical erect tillering grass, 60–120 cm tall
habitat_and_climate: Cool winter temperate to subtropical zones, bright sunny days during grain fill
water_requirements: Moderate; 4–6 irrigations at CRI, tillering, jointing, flowering stages
soil_preferences: Well-drained fertile loamy to clay loam alluvial soils, pH 6.0–7.5
uses: Staple food grain consumed as chapati, roti, bread, semolina
Wheat bran as nutritious cattle feed
safety_notes: Contains gluten. Individuals with celiac disease must avoid ingestion.

common_pests_and_diseases.name: Stripe / Yellow Rust (Puccinia striiformis)
common_pests_and_diseases.symptoms: Bright yellow pustules arranged in linear stripes on leaf blades
common_pests_and_diseases.management: Foliar spray of Propiconazole 25 EC (0.1%)

common_pests_and_diseases.name: Leaf / Brown Rust (Puccinia triticina)
common_pests_and_diseases.symptoms: Small round-to-oval orange-brown pustules scattered across leaves
common_pests_and_diseases.management: Sow resistant cultivars (DBW 187, HD 3086); apply Tilt 25 EC

prevention_guidance: Sow early in November for optimal vernalization
Ensure first irrigation at Crown Root Initiation (CRI) 21 days after sowing
Avoid excessive nitrogen late in season to prevent lodging

leaf_characteristics.shape: Bipinnate feathery compound leaves with 3–6 pairs of pinnae and 10–25 pairs of minute oblong leaflets; sharp paired straight white stipular spines at nodes

stem_characteristics: Stout, crooked trunk with blackish deeply fissured rough bark and rounded crown, 6–15 m
flower_characteristics: Globose fluffy bright golden-yellow fragrant flower heads clustered in leaf axils
fruit_characteristics: Constricted, deeply lobed grey-white felted indehiscent pod (necklace-like necklace pod, 10–15 cm) with brown seeds
growth_habit: Hardy spiny evergreen or semi-deciduous tree, 6–15 meters
habitat_and_climate: Arid and semi-arid desert plains, black cotton soil tracts, and saline wastelands; heat and drought champion
water_requirements: Low; exceptional drought hardiness; tolerates seasonal flooding
soil_preferences: Deep black cotton soils, saline-alkaline tracts, and gravelly alluvium, pH 6.5–9.0
growing_season: Flowering in monsoon (June–Sept), pods ripen in winter
propagation_methods: Seeds (presoaked in sulfuric acid or cow dung slurry)
uses: Ayurvedic dental twig (babool datun) for oral hygiene and gum strengthening
High-tannin bark used for leather tanning
Nutritious protein pods and foliage for goats and camels in arid zones
Natural Gum Arabic (babul gond) used in sweets (gond ke laddu) and pharmaceuticals
safety_notes: Sharp straight white thorns (1–5 cm long). Wear thick gloves when handling.

common_pests_and_diseases.symptoms: White fungal coating on young leaves
common_pests_and_diseases.management: Natural tolerance in arid conditions

prevention_guidance: Outstanding species for reclaiming degraded sodic soils and barren ravines

leaf_characteristics.shape: Trifoliolate compound leaves with densely hairy ovate leaflets
leaf_characteristics.color: Dark green with coarse bristly hairs

stem_characteristics: Diffusely branched erect to spreading hairy stem, 30–70 cm
flower_characteristics: Bright yellow papilionaceous flowers in compact axillary racemes
fruit_characteristics: Short erect cylindrical hairy pods holding 6–10 cylindrical black seeds with white concave hilum
growth_habit: Erect or spreading annual herb, 30–75 cm
habitat_and_climate: Warm sub-humid to humid tropical plains; 70–85 day maturity
water_requirements: Low to moderate
soil_preferences: Black cotton soils and heavy loams with good drainage, pH 6.5–7.8
uses: Essential ingredient for idli, dosa, vada, dal makhani (contains high mucilaginous protein)
Enriches soil through biological nitrogen fixation
safety_notes: Safe for consumption.

common_pests_and_diseases.name: Powdery Mildew (Erysiphe polygoni)
common_pests_and_diseases.symptoms: White flour-like powdery fungal coating on upper leaf surfaces and pods
common_pests_and_diseases.management: Foliar spray of Wettable Sulfur (2 g/L) or Hexaconazole

prevention_guidance: Sow in rice fallows with zero tillage to utilize residual moisture
Treat seeds with Trichoderma (4 g/kg)

leaf_characteristics.shape: Trifoliolate ovate leaflets with acute tips

stem_characteristics: Herbaceous furrowed erect or semi-erect branching stem, 30–75 cm
flower_characteristics: Clusters of pale yellow papilionaceous flowers on axillary racemes
fruit_characteristics: Slender cylindrical hairy pods, 6–10 cm long, turning dark brown/black when ripe with 10–15 green seeds
growth_habit: Erect bushy annual legume, 30–80 cm tall
habitat_and_climate: Warm tropical and subtropical seasons; rapid 60–75 day maturation cycle
water_requirements: Moderate; thrives in Kharif and Summer under light irrigation
soil_preferences: Well-drained sandy loam to fertile alluvial loam, pH 6.2–7.5
uses: Highly digestible protein-rich pulse; whole moong sprouts, yellow dal
Green manure crop fixing 35–40 kg N/ha

common_pests_and_diseases.name: Yellow Mosaic Virus (MYMV)
common_pests_and_diseases.symptoms: Irregular bright yellow and green mosaic patches on leaves
common_pests_and_diseases.management: Control whitefly vector with Thiamethoxam 25 WG (0.3 g/L); cultivate resistant varieties (IPM 02-3)

prevention_guidance: Seed treatment with Rhizobium and PSB biofertilizers
Harvest when 80% pods turn brown-black to avoid shattering

leaf_characteristics.shape: Large, cordate palmately 3–5 lobed leaves with coarsely serrate margins

stem_characteristics: Woody climbing deciduous vine with leaf-opposed branched coiled tendrils, up to 15 m
flower_characteristics: Dense panicles of tiny yellowish-green fragrant flowers
fruit_characteristics: Globose to ellipsoid fleshy juicy berries in tight pendulous bunches (green, purple, red, black)
growth_habit: Vigorous woody perennial climbing liana, trained on overhead pandals, 3–15 m
habitat_and_climate: Warm dry Mediterranean to subtropical climate; dry rainless sunny weather during berry ripening is essential
water_requirements: Controlled drip irrigation; withholding water before harvest enhances Brix sugars
soil_preferences: Deep, well-drained sandy loam or gravelly loam soils, pH 6.5–7.8
growing_season: Double pruning system: Foundation pruning (April) and Forward fruiting pruning (October)
propagation_methods: Hardwood cuttings grafted on Dog Ridge rootstock (Thomson Seedless, Sonaka, Sharad Seedless)
uses: Fresh table fruit, sweet raisins (kishmish), premium wine production
Grape seed oil and resveratrol antioxidant extract
safety_notes: Safe for human consumption. TOXIC to dogs (causes acute kidney failure).

common_pests_and_diseases.name: Downy Mildew (Plasmopara viticola)
common_pests_and_diseases.symptoms: Yellowish translucent 'oil spots' on upper leaf surface with dense white cottony fungal growth on underside
common_pests_and_diseases.management: Spray Bordeaux mixture 1% or Metalaxyl + Mancozeb (2.5 g/L)

common_pests_and_diseases.name: Powdery Mildew (Uncinula necator)
common_pests_and_diseases.symptoms: Ash-grey powdery coating on leaves and young berries causing berry cracking
common_pests_and_diseases.management: Foliar sulfur dust or Azoxystrobin (1 ml/L)

prevention_guidance: Train on Bower / Pergola trellises for optimal airflow and sunlight interception
Dip developing bunches in Gibberellic Acid (GA3 @ 10–40 ppm) for berry elongation

leaf_characteristics.shape: Simple, ovate to elliptic dull green leaves covered with fine starry tomentose hairs with characteristic horse-like aroma

stem_characteristics: Erect, branching tomentose semi-woody shrub with pale green-brown stem, 30–120 cm
flower_characteristics: Small greenish-yellow bell-shaped flowers clustered in axils (3–6 flowers)
fruit_characteristics: Globose smooth berry (6 mm), bright orange-red when ripe, enclosed inside an enlarged papery inflated calyx
growth_habit: Erect branching semi-woody perennial shrub grown as annual, 30–120 cm
habitat_and_climate: Semi-arid subtropical and tropical dry climate; dry weather required for root development
water_requirements: Low; highly drought hardy
soil_preferences: Well-drained light sandy loam or red gravelly soils, pH 7.0–8.0
growing_season: Late Kharif sowing (July–August), harvested 150–180 days in winter (JA-20, Poshita)
uses: Premier Ayurvedic adaptogen: reduces cortisol stress, enhances vitality and endurance (withanolides)
Tuberous roots dried and powdered for medicinal formulations
Leaves used in traditional poultices for joint swelling
safety_notes: Roots have strong adaptogenic potency; pregnant women should avoid unprescribed medicinal doses.

common_pests_and_diseases.name: Seedling Blight (Alternaria alternata)
common_pests_and_diseases.symptoms: Brown circular spots on leaves and seedling damping-off
common_pests_and_diseases.management: Seed treatment with Trichoderma (4 g/kg)

prevention_guidance: Harvest roots when berries turn orange-red and leaves begin drying
Grade roots based on diameter (A, B, C grade)

leaf_characteristics.shape: Large broad linear-lanceolate arched blades

stem_characteristics: Stout, solid unbranched erect stem with prominent prop/stilt roots at basal nodes
flower_characteristics: Monoecious: male tassel at stem apex, female ear (cob) in leaf axils with silks
fruit_characteristics: Cylindrical cob with 12–20 rows of yellow, white, or golden kernels
growth_habit: Stout robust annual erect C4 grass, 1.5–3.0 meters tall
habitat_and_climate: Warm tropical and sub-tropical plains and plateaus
water_requirements: Moderate; sensitive to both drought and waterlogging
soil_preferences: Deep fertile well-drained sandy loam to clay loam, pH 6.5–7.5
uses: Human food (corn flour, sweet corn, popcorn)
Poultry and livestock feed
Starch and biofuel production
safety_notes: Safe for human and animal consumption.

common_pests_and_diseases.name: Fall Armyworm (Spodoptera frugiperda)
common_pests_and_diseases.symptoms: Pin-holes, large irregular windowpane feeding on whorl leaves with sawdust frass
common_pests_and_diseases.management: Whorl application of Emamectin benzoate 5% SG (0.4 g/L) or Chlorantraniliprole

common_pests_and_diseases.name: Turcicum Leaf Blight (Exserohilum turcicum)
common_pests_and_diseases.symptoms: Long elliptical boat-shaped greyish-green lesions on lower leaves
common_pests_and_diseases.management: Spray Mancozeb (2.5 g/L) at first symptom appearance

prevention_guidance: Install pheromone traps (5/acre) for FAW monitoring
Practice ridge and furrow planting for drainage
Provide split nitrogen at knee-high and tasseling stages

leaf_characteristics.shape: Linear-lanceolate smooth grass-like leaves with sheathing bases arising from underground aromatic rhizome
leaf_characteristics.color: Deep glossy green with distinct spicy scent

stem_characteristics: Slender leafy pseudostem formed by leaf sheaths, 60–100 cm tall, rising from subterranean branched tuberous rhizome
flower_characteristics: Dense conical spike with green bracts and yellowish-green flowers with purple lips (rarely blooms)
fruit_characteristics: Vegetatively propagated via rhizomes
growth_habit: Erect perennial rhizomatous herb grown as annual, 60–100 cm
habitat_and_climate: Warm humid tropical and sub-tropical climate with abundant rainfall and warm shade
sunlight_requirements: Partial shade (thrives under 25–50% shade or agroforestry intercropping)
water_requirements: High; regular soil moisture essential; highly sensitive to waterlogging
soil_preferences: Rich, loose, well-drained friable sandy loam or forest loam high in organic humus, pH 5.5–6.8
growing_season: Planted with pre-monsoon showers (April–May), harvested at 8–10 months (IISR Rejatha, Varada, Mahima)
propagation_methods: Rhizome seed pieces (bits) with 1–2 viable sprouts
uses: Essential aromatic culinary rhizome (adrak chai, ginger garlic paste, curries)
Medicinal: gingerol and shogaol soothe nausea, morning sickness, digestive indigestion, and throat irritation
Dry ginger (sonth) for spice blends
safety_notes: Safe for human nutrition.

common_pests_and_diseases.name: Soft Rot / Rhizome Rot (Pythium myriotylum)
common_pests_and_diseases.symptoms: Water-soaked basal leaf sheaths, yellowing and sudden wilting of tillers, foul soft rot of underground rhizome
common_pests_and_diseases.management: Seed rhizome dip in Metalaxyl (2 g/L); drench affected beds; ensure high raised beds

prevention_guidance: Plant on 15–20 cm raised beds to ensure rapid excess water drainage
Mulch with 12 t/ha green tree leaves in three split applications

common_name: Indian Jujube / Ber / Poor Man's Apple

leaf_characteristics.shape: Small, ovate to elliptic glossy dark green leaves, densely covered with white/buff felted tomentum beneath
leaf_characteristics.color: Glossy dark green above, whitish woolly beneath

stem_characteristics: Spreading thorny shrub or small tree with zigzag branchlets and sharp paired stipular spines (one straight, one hooked), 4–10 m
flower_characteristics: Small inconspicuous greenish-yellow fragrant flowers in axillary cymes
fruit_characteristics: Globose to oblong fleshy drupe (2–5 cm) with smooth shiny skin, green turning golden-yellow to reddish-brown; sweet-sour pulp with hard stone
growth_habit: Extremely hardy spiny evergreen or semi-deciduous tree, 4–10 meters
habitat_and_climate: Arid and semi-arid desert climate; extreme drought hardiness and heat tolerance (up to 48°C)
water_requirements: Very low; survives where other fruit trees fail
soil_preferences: Tolerates poor soils: sandy, gravelly, saline, and alkaline soils, pH 6.5–9.0
growing_season: Winter harvest (December–March) (Gola, Seb, Umran, Kaithli, Apple Ber)
propagation_methods: Ring budding or shield budding on wild Ziziphus rotundifolia rootstock
uses: Poor man's apple: eaten fresh, dried, candies, and pickles
Valuable source of Vitamin C and minerals in desert ecosystems
Host plant for lac insects (Kerria lacca) and silkworms; dry spiny branches for livestock fencing
safety_notes: Sharp paired hooked spines require careful manual picking. Safe.

common_pests_and_diseases.name: Powdery Mildew (Oidium erysiphoides f. sp. ziziphi)
common_pests_and_diseases.symptoms: White powdery fungal growth on developing fruits causing skin corking and fruit drop
common_pests_and_diseases.management: Spray Wettable Sulfur (2 g/L) or Dinocap during marble stage

prevention_guidance: Annual severe pruning in May–June is essential to stimulate vigorous new fruiting wood for winter crop
